why: Both land on the key's hedgehog (paper-based consumer products, profit per consumer brand, exit the commodity mills), but Analysis 2 explicitly calls for selling the namesake mill and redeploying the proceeds, has a tighter verdict, and adds a fallback and dated 90-day actions. Analysis 1 states the mills-as-commodity-capital-trap fact more directly and avoids the extrapolated figures (0.67x, 3x) that Analysis 2 introduces, even though those are flagged as assumptions.
